why: Third point of the rewalked lambda curve, and a prediction written before the run. ci-88 at lambda 0.9 is the first agent here to beat search-4 measurably -- win rate 0.6550 over 400 matches, interval 0.5988 to 0.7112, the whole of it above one half -- and it loses to Greedy 0.0325, where search-4 beats Greedy 0.930. So it is an exploit of one opponent rather than a better player, and the Greedy bar refused it. Against lambda 0.95 (ci-86, reproduced by ci-87) the two opponents order the two lambdas in opposite directions and not narrowly: 0.95 is 26 points better against Greedy, 0.9 is 17 points better against search-4. Lowering lambda buys specialisation against the teacher and pays for it everywhere else. The mechanism is the round cap, and only against search-4: 17.1 rounds with 38.2% capped there, against 7.0 rounds and 0.0% capped against Greedy, which is the Greedy mirror's own pace, with spell entropy 2.42 and a 15.6% fizzle rate. ADR 0011 hands a capped match to the healthier team. This turn moves one knob, lambda 0.9 to 0.8. The prediction: if the trend is monotone, 0.8 is worse still against Greedy and better still against search-4; if instead 0.9 is a peak against search-4, it is a resonance with the teacher rather than a trend. Either answer is worth the run. Expect the clone identical again and refused again at 0.5 against models/clone/ci-69. Still open: reading the capped matches apart from the decided ones, which is the measurement that would settle the stalling story rather than infer it; a second independent opponent that is not the teacher; and the nonlinear baseline ADR 0048 left on the table.
